# trace-analysis.v2.md

**Status:** Supersedes `trace-analysis.v1.md`. Test 1 post-mortem, deep edition.
**Basis:** `corpus_trace.v1.txt` (12,862 decisions) × `prose-corpus.md` × `suppression-spec.md` v1.2 × `suppression_splitter.v1.py`. Same trace as v1 — regenerated byte-identically and re-certified (§1).
**Scope:** measurement only. No implementation is proposed or written. Every claim cites a spec rule ID or a measured quantity with provenance class (Appendix A). Notation: `⏎` = newline, `‖` = trace decision point.

---

## §0 Executive verdict

v1 said: *W1 held; the failure is recall and corpus fit.* That verdict survives — but it was built on three estimates, one unreproducible count, and one doctrinal assumption. v2 replaces all of them with measurements, and the picture is sharper:

1. **W1 holds as a doctrine, and now as a measurement.** Split-side precision is **8,918 / 9,089 = 98.12%** (rule-of-three floor ≥ 96.2% at 95% confidence). Every one of the 171 false splits passes through a door §6 already declares: **159 through Door A(ii)** (enumerator/label orphans), **12 through Door A(i)** (one family: `conc.` before a chemical). Doors B and C: **zero** violations. No W1 falsification candidate exists in the trace.
2. **The suppression stack is mis-calibrated for this genre, now measured rule by rule.** R1.2 — the modal suppressor — is **665 correct / 2,021 false merges (24.8% / 75.2%)**, replacing v1's ~770/~1,900 estimate. Outside R1.2, the in-scope keeps are **~810 of 1,087 (~75%) wrong-direction** (R3.1 177/206 wrong; R1.3 154/155 wrong; KEEP-DL5 sampled at 33.3% precision; R2.1 4/7 wrong; R4.2 10/19 wrong).
3. **The largest pathology source is upstream of the entire rule stack.** Of 10,492 terminator-less output chunks, **89.6% are manufactured by the blank-line block layer alone** (D12), 6.5% by keep-refusals, 3.9% by logged splits. The spec has no ingestion layer; the block layer adjudicates 100% of the corpus as prose, but only **66.1% of input blocks are prose** (§7).
4. **Recall now has a number** (v1 had none): pooled expert-reader recall on sampled prose blocks = **0.837** (95% CI [0.727, 0.948]); per-genre 1.000 study-guide / 0.714 exam-readiness / 0.857 reference. Misses concentrate at part-label glue (R3.1) and at boundaries the candidate machinery never sees (terminator-less single-`⏎` breaks — again ingestion).

The one-line summary: **the architecture did its job; the accepted-miss schedule was calibrated for the wrong genre; and nine tenths of the visible damage happens before any rule fires.**

---

## §1 Method and reproducibility

- **Regeneration certified three ways:** the trace regenerates byte-identically from `suppression_splitter.v1.py --trace` + `prose-corpus.md`; all 12,862 context windows independently re-derived from a from-scratch tokenizer replica match 12,862/12,862; the committed trace parses 12,862/12,862 under the line grammar with zero anomalies (no unparsed lines, no empty contexts, no duplicate offsets, strictly increasing offsets, min 197, max 1,692,981).
- **Character accounting (fixes a v1 conflation):** the corpus is **1,693,006 characters** (1,748,367 **bytes**). All trace offsets are character offsets. v1's chunk-length statistics were computed in bytes and reported as chars (§9).
- **Candidate density:** 759.7 candidates per 100k characters overall.
- **v1's forensic protocol is upgraded to a six-workstream census** (quantitative census / split-side audit / R1.2 census / small-rule forensics / output-block pathology / corpus anatomy + delta impact & recall), each with full-population measurement where feasible and seed-42 sampling with Wilson CIs where not. Provenance classes are defined in Appendix A and attached to every number below.
- **Adjudication standard:** a decision is CORRECT iff a physics-teacher reader agrees a real sentence boundary exists (SPLIT) or does not exist (KEEP) at that point. Abbreviation-internal dots (`p.d.`, `e.g.`) are not boundaries.

## §2 Decision and output arithmetic

### 2.1 Decision census (exact)

| Decision | Rule label | Count | Share |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| SPLIT | DL1+DL5 | 4,722 | 36.7% |
| SPLIT | DL3 | 4,367 | 34.0% |
| KEEP | R1.2 | 2,686 | 20.9% |
| KEEP | DL5 | 700 | 5.4% |
| KEEP | R3.1 | 206 | 1.6% |
| KEEP | R1.3 | 155 | 1.2% |
| KEEP | R4.2 | 19 | 0.15% |
| KEEP | R2.1 | 7 | 0.05% |
| **Total** | | **12,862** | |

### 2.2 What the labels actually mean (new — v1 reported them without semantics)

From the implementation's control flow (line refs from `suppression_splitter.v1.py`):

- **`DL3` is decided before the suppression stack runs** (L256–260): if the candidate token is the block's last token, the block-edge override fires and `decide()` is never called. This is why DL3 rows never display an R-rule — the R-conditions were not evaluated. **All 4,367 DL3 splits are at code block edges** (audit in §3.3).
- **`DL1+DL5` is a conjunction, not a sum.** The only in-block SPLIT path (L320–321) requires *all* suppression rules to fail **and** the next token's effective initial to be uppercase. A DL1-only or DL5-only split is unreachable in this trace: DL1 (word-shape license) and DL5 (terminator license) always fire jointly or not at all. v1's "DL1+DL5" phrasing was numerically right but semantically unexplained.
- **`KEEP DL5` is the fall-through suppression label** (L322): the next token's initial is *not* uppercase, and no R-rule claimed the keep. The 700 decompose exactly into **571 digit-initial** continuations and **129 symbol-initial** continuations (`−`×36, `□`×35, `+`×11, `├──`×9, `|`×8, `/`×8, `→`×6 …) — zero have no following token. Under spec v1.2 these 700 would be cited to **R3.1** (lowercase/digit/symbol continuation) — pure citation drift (δ7, §8), zero outcome change.
- R1.1 never fires (dead code path); R3.2 never fires (withdrawn rule, §8).

### 2.3 Output arithmetic (new — reconciled exactly)

v1 counted 22,257 output chunks but never reconciled them against 9,089 logged splits (naive slices: 9,090). The reconciliation:

**22,257 = 17,535 block tails + 4,722 in-block split pieces + 0 + 0**

- **17,535** = one tail per non-empty input block (17,534 blank-line runs → 17,535 blocks, zero whitespace-only lines). These tails are **never logged in the trace** — 13,168 structural cuts are invisible in the decision stream.
- **4,722** = in-block pieces cut by DL1+DL5 splits.
- **DL3 emits nothing.** The 4,367 DL3 decisions *certify* tails that the block layer cuts anyway; zero chunks start at a DL3 offset. The trace's most numerous split license is, at output level, a no-op — its real function is logging.
- There is **no newline splitting**: D12 makes a single `⏎` ordinary whitespace inside a block (verified — no code path splits on it; consequence in §6/§11).

## §3 The split side (new — v1 assumed, v2 measures)

v1 asserted W1 from doctrine and spot checks. v2 audits the split population directly.

### 3.1 Per-class full-population audit

Every SPLIT was pulled with ±80 chars of context and class-swept by pre-token shape. Classes with ≤100 members were adjudicated 100%; larger classes by seed-42 n=50 samples (Wilson 95% CI).

| Pre-token class | Members | Adjudication | Precision | Wilson 95% CI |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| single letter + `.` (`d.`, `V.`) | 132 | 50 sampled, all correct | 100% | [92.9–100] |
| dotted-abbreviation tail (`p.d.`, `e.m.f.`) | 20 | 20/20 correct | 100% | [83.9–100] |
| ALL-CAPS ≤5 (units/codes) | 412 | 50 sampled, all correct | 100% | [92.9–100] |
| danger-list words (`vs.`, `No.`, `Fig.`…) | 24 | 12/24 correct | **50%** | [31.4–68.6] |
| lone digit (`7.`, `N.`) | 66 | 66/66 correct | 100% | [94.5–100] |

- The danger-list failures are **one family**: `conc. ‖ H₂SO₄ / HCl / H₃PO₄` — the concentration abbreviation followed by a chemical formula, split as if a sentence ended at `conc.`. 14 splits in the family, 12 false / 2 correct. Textbook **Door A(i)**: a plain-shaped abbreviation absent from Set P.
- A ~90-member rare-abbreviation sweep (`nm. hf. vt. mg. kg. rad. min. sat. MS. spec. rtp. atm. mm.` …) found **zero** false splits.

### 3.2 Door B (attribution gap) — recount and audit

Splits whose pre-context ends with `"`: **247 exactly** (81 DL3 + 166 in-block); including curly `”`: **269**. A 30-sample adjudication found **30/30 correct** [88.7–100]. The corpus's pattern is quoted model-answers followed by examiner commentary (`…hydrolysis?" ‖ Answer: The C–Cl bo…`), not dialogue — so the attribution guard correctly stays out of the way. **v1's count of 146 is not reproducible** under any of 15 reconstruction variants and is hereby corrected (see §9).

### 3.3 DL3 audit — clean

All 4,367 DL3 splits sit at code block edges (blank line = `\n{2,}`; single `⏎` is *not* an edge — spec-D12-conformant). The corpus contains 0 whitespace-only lines and 0 markup block tags, so **zero DL3 splits diverge from a spec block edge**. Nothing to repair here.

### 3.4 Em dash (ruling (d)) — measured, and benign

v1 flagged ruling (d) (`word—Next` = one token) as an undeclared glue class and bounded it at ~47. Measured: the corpus contains **3,184 `—`**, of which **99.3% are spaced** (separate token — no fusion possible) and only **21 are word-adjacent**, all of them chemistry bond notation (`O—H`, `H—O—CH₂—CH₂—CH₃`) where fusion is *desirable*. **Zero candidates defeated, zero false merges.** The ruling (d) concern is real in theory but has no footprint on this corpus (§9, correction 6).

### 3.5 Verdict

**Split-side precision: 8,918/9,089 = 98.12%** (floor ≥ 96.2% @95%). All 171 false splits: 159 × Door A(ii), 12 × Door A(i), 0 × Door B, 0 × Door C. **W1 stands — as a conditional claim, with its doors now holding measured leak rates.** TheDoor A(ii) leak is the spec's own predicted family (`10. Foo` enumerators) and is the subject of §11-R6.

## §4 The keep side (measured rule by rule)

A KEEP at a terminator candidate is a refused split; when a real sentence ends there it is a **false merge**. This is where the genre mismatch lives.

### 4.1 R1.2 — the modal suppression, fully censused (2,686 keeps)

The rule keys on a **single-character word-token immediately left of the candidate period**. The complete census: **63 distinct pre-tokens**, all 2,686 rows classified with context-verified adjudication (top-40 tokens ×3 contexts each; every lowercase-next and symbol-next row read individually).

| Class | Correct | False merge | Total |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| (i) dotted-abbreviation tail letters | 646 | 32 | 678 |
| (ii) unit/variable letters (`A V C m l r D`…) | 5 | 420 | 425 |
| (iii) digits (enumerators & math ends) | 0 | 1,556 | 1,556 |
| (iv) symbols/other (`+ Ω λ θ ² ₂`…) | 14 | 13 | 27 |
| **Total** | **665 (24.8%)** | **2,021 (75.2%)** | **2,686** |

- **Measured inventory of dotted abbreviations in the corpus** (case-sensitive): `p.d.`×367 (+`P.D.`×28), `e.g.`×235 (+`E.g.`×2), `e.m.f.`×149, `s.f.`×33, `b.p.`×18, `i.e.`×19, plus `e.m.f.s.`×3, `m.f.`×1. **`r.m.s.`, `d.c.`, `a.c.` occur zero times** — the corpus's dotted-abbreviation world is exactly six families plus two rare variants.
- The 646 correct keeps are the tails of those families. The 32 false ones are family-final occurrences (`…NOT the e.m.f. ‖ The e.m.f. must…`) — sentence-final dotted abbreviations, i.e. **AM-2's residual is real but tiny: 32 rows**.
- **The false-merge mass is digits and units.** Worst tokens: `2`×309, `1`×305, `3`×279, `4`×210, `5`×146, `6`×103, `7`×76, `8`×59, `A`×53, `9`×43, `V`×41, `Ω`×31, `C`×27, `d`×26, `m`×26. Within the 1,556 digit false merges: **1,107 line-start enumerators** (`2. ‖ Calculate…`) and **449 math/number sentence-ends** (`…= 16.0 V. ‖ 16.0 + 8.0 = 24 V`).
- **Design consequence (feeds §11-R2):** a tail-whitelist limited to the six observed families would preserve ~97% of R1.2's correct keeps (646/665) while licensing splits for the 1,976 digit/letter false merges — i.e., the fix is not "make R1.2 smarter" but "**move digits/units from the KEEP side to the SPLIT side**".
- Implementation quirk (D6 divergence): the impl's single-char rule also fires on symbols (`+ = | ↑ ↓ ½ ✓`) and Unicode subscript/superscript digits (`² ₂`) — spec v1.2 D6 restricts it to Letter ∪ Digit. Sixteen in-block symbol candidates are KEPT by the impl where v1.2 would split (§8-δ6).
- R1.2 is also cited on 18 ellipsis-cluster keeps that belong to R4.2 (citation drift inside the keep side).

### 4.2 R3.1 — lowercase continuation (206 keeps): 85.9% wrong

| Sub-class | Count | Verdict |
|---|---:|---|
| part-label glue: `(a)`–`(d)` ×122, roman `(i)/(ii)/(iii)` ×22 | 144 | all wrong — stems glued to sub-parts |
| symbol/formula continuation | 33 | all wrong |
| genuine continuations (quote-pair glue, parentheticals, `e.g./etc/Est.`) | 29 | correct |

Worst verbatim: `…wrong with this answer? ⏎ (ii) What should…` · `…has the student made? ⏎ (ii) What should they have drawn…` · `…measured from the normal. ⏎ (b) Calculate the critical angle…`. The 29 correct continuations are the reason this rule cannot simply be deleted — it needs re-scoping, not removal (§11-R3).

### 4.3 R1.3 — all-caps/internal-period token rule (155 keeps): 99.4% wrong

Census of the 74 distinct pre-tokens: formula quantities ×40 (`ΔT`×7, `ΔH`×6, `ΔE`×4, `V/W/Q/I²R/V²/R` families), chemical formulas ×40 (`H₂O`, `KOH`, `NH₄NO₃`…), acronyms/labels ×55 (`QWC`×12, `CP`×13, `LDR`×8, `EMF`×8, `WPH12`×3), caps-emphasis ×20 (`DECREASES`, `WRONG`, `ONLY`). **154 of 155 are false merges** (only survivor: a `(2 marks)` annotation row). Worst: `…in a circuit: V = W/Q. ⏎ It is the energy lost…` · `…derived using V = IR. ⏎ 69 — ⏎ P = I²R…`.

### 4.4 R2.1 — Set P dictionary (7 keeps): 4 wrong, 3 right (v1 verified)

- Wrong (namespace collisions): `No.` (numero ↔ the answer-word "No"), `Ca.` (circa ↔ element symbol), `sat.` (Saturday ↔ participle of *sit*), `ms.` (honorific ↔ millisecond unit).
- Right: `pp.` ×3 (genuine page-range internal dots).
- New conformance finding: the impl's P set is missing v1.2's `gov`/`al` entries → ruling 7.32 (`Gov. Smith`) fails live. `--strict-asterisks` also remains an L5 violation (§8-δ1).

### 4.5 R4.2 — ellipsis cluster (19 keeps): 10 wrong / 9 right

Wrong: enumeration ellipses that end sentences (`n = 1, 2, 3, … ⏎ The n-th harmonic…`) and truncated TOC rows. Right: path-diff table rows, quoted titles, `(CPx style)` tags.

### 4.6 KEEP DL5 — the fall-through (700 keeps): sampled precision 33.3%

571 digit-initial + 129 symbol-initial continuations (§2.2). Terminators: `.`×627, `?`×73, zero `!`, zero raw ellipses (R4.2 pre-empts those). Seed-42 n=30 adjudication: **10 right / 20 wrong → 33.3% [Wilson 19.2–51.2]**. False-merge modes: marks-table debris (`…r = (ε − V)/I. ⏎ 78 First explicitly tested…`) and numbered-checklist fusion (`1. Read the whole answer. ⏎ 2. Count the IC points…`).

### 4.7 Aggregate

Excluding R1.2, the in-scope keep population is 1,087 (700+206+155+19+7), of which **~810 (~75%) are wrong-direction**. Including R1.2: **~2,830 of 3,773 keeps (~75%) suppress a real boundary.** The suppression stack is not "conservative" on this corpus — it is mostly wrong, because it was designed for prose punctuation hazards (titles, honorifics, page numbers) that this corpus barely contains (Set P fired 7 times total; `No.` ×1), while adjudicating thousands of digits, units, and labels it was never scheduled to see.

## §5 Recall (new — v1 had no number)

Method: 45 prose blocks sampled seed-42 across three genres (15 each: study-guide, exam-readiness, reference); every true boundary marked by expert reading; HIT = a logged SPLIT within ±2 chars.

| Genre | True boundaries | Hits | Recall |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| study-guide (ch2.7) | 15 | 15 | 1.000 |
| exam-readiness (ch2.8) | 21 | 15 | 0.714 |
| reference (waves-quanta) | 7 | 6 | 0.857 |
| **Pooled** | **43** | **36** | **0.837** (95% CI [0.727, 0.948]) |

- **Miss owners (7 misses):** part-label glue ×3 (`…answer. ⏎ (a)/(b)…` — R3.1 keeps); **no-candidate/no-license ×4** — boundaries at terminator-less single-`⏎` breaks (`increases⏎Note:`, `(1 mark)⏎Note:`, `H₂O(l)⏎Explain`, callout-title glue) where the candidate machinery never fires because D12 does not treat a single newline as structure. That is an **ingestion-layer miss, not a rule miss**.
- Sampled precision on the same blocks: **36/36 = 1.000** — on true prose, punctuated in-block adjudication is effectively perfect. (This does not contradict the 171 false splits of §3: the sampler landed on prose blocks, not on label debris.)

## §6 Output pathology and causal attribution

### 6.1 Chunk taxonomy (all 22,257 chunks, precedence-ordered primary class)

| Primary class | Chunks | | Overlapping flag | Chunks |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|
| plain prose | 10,234 | | ends without terminator | 10,492 (47.1%) |
| no-terminator (primary) | 8,668 | | starts with enumerator | 1,063 |
| starts with enumerator | 1,048 | | contains table pipes | 154 |
| heading (`#…`) | 2,071 | | diagram debris | 75 |
| pure label (`10.`, `(a)`, `M3`…) | 54 | | | |
| table row / diagram / empty | 152 / 30 / 0 | | | |

Length (characters, correct units): mean 74.3, p50/p90/p99 = 58 / 152 / 318, max 1,121. (In collapsed bytes: mean 76.6 — v1's "avg 77 chars" was bytes; ">300" ×300 was bytes too.) The ten shortest chunks are **length-1 whole blocks**: `× B B B N ☰ ☰ ☽ ☾ ↓` — UI chrome from the source pages.

### 6.2 The attribution crosstab (the new key table)

For every terminator-less chunk, what *created* it?

| Creator | Heading | Table | Diagram | Enum | No-term | **Total** |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **(b) structural block tail — no trace decision involved** | 1,313 | 56 | 12 | 0 | 8,019 | **9,400 = 89.6%** |
| **(c) tail after a KEEP refused** (within 200 chars) | 154 | 7 | 5 | 269 | 246 | **681 = 6.5%** |
| **(a) born at a logged SPLIT** (all DL1+DL5) | 0 | 2 | 3 | 0 | 400 | **405 = 3.9%** |

(b)∩(c) overlap 141. Refusal breakdown for (c): **R1.2 ×516, DL5 ×149, R1.3 ×8, R3.1 ×8**.

**Reading:** the blank-line block layer alone manufactures ~90% of the furniture the output is blamed for. Even deleting every suppression rule would leave the output overwhelmingly non-prose. Conversely, the rules' *output-visible* damage (405 + 681 chunks) is real but secondary — and of that, R1.2 is again the largest single contributor.

Caveats measured: **zero real pipe-delimited data tables remain** — the 156 multi-pipe lines are Hess cycles / wavefront ASCII / `|V|` absolute values, because the HTML→markdown extraction flattened ~400 real tables into prose-shaped lines; 84 UI-chrome blocks (`☰ 🌙 📊 ✕`, 2,348 chars) ride along as "prose".

### 7.2 Where it hurts (per-section)

Worst furniture shares (by chars): `unit2-formula-sheet` 61.4% · `ext-synoptic` 53.1% · `ext-uncertainty` 47.4% · `ch2.3-exam-readiness` 43.4% · `ext-cp4-8-methods` 41.9%. By genre: methods 41.9% > reference 40.5% > formula-atlas 36.3% > study-guide 31.9% > memorization 30.8% > exam-readiness 28.8% > past-paper-index 15.6%.

### 7.3 Decision stream vs corpus classes

**5,044 of 12,862 decisions (39.2%) sit in furniture** (label 3,506 · formula 964 · heading 363 · table 176 · diagram 35). Keep-rate by class: heading 76.0% · diagram 88.6% · table 44.3% · label 43.5% · formula 28.5% · **prose 20.3%**. The realistic in-prose candidate universe (`\.(?=\s+[A-Z0-9"'(])` inside prose blocks) is **3,969 candidates** — the trace's 12,862 decisions are adjudicating a stream three times larger than the prose it exists for.

### 7.4 Hazard census (measured, whole corpus)

p.d. 367 (+P.D. 28) · e.g. 235 · e.m.f. 149 · s.f. 33 · b.p. 18 · i.e. 19 · r.m.s./d.c./a.c. **0** · single-letter+period 410 (337 excluding abbrev tails) · line-start enumerators 1,136 (all `N.`-form) vs mid-line 2,130 · `(a–h)` labels 736 · `Q\d+` 3,250 · `Spec ref:` 204 · `✓` 114 · `MS:` 72 · `NN MM marks` glue 272 · `).` 1,928 · decimals 6,375 · quotes 3,901+400 · ellipses 72+55 · `etc.` 11 · `No.` 1 · `—` 3,184 (99.3% spaced) · `**` 4 chars (2 spans).

## §8 Spec-conformance deltas, quantified (v1 listed seven; v1 never priced them)

| # | Delta (impl → v1.2) | Footprint on this trace | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `--strict-asterisks` (L5 violation) | 5 rows re-cite; 0 outcome changes | inert but non-conformant |
| 2 | R3.2 alive (withdrawn in v1.2) | 0 would-fires (replica-instrumented) | fully dormant |
| 3 | BLOCK_TAGS missing `th` | `<th` ×0 in corpus; 0 header rows at risk | zero impact here |
| 4 | ws-only lines not blank (D12) | 0 whitespace-only lines in corpus | moot (latent risk) |
| 5 | T3 skip-all-punctuation vs opening-only | 0 divergent candidates | zero impact |
| 6 | **D6 lone symbols treated as single chars** | **16 decisions: impl KEEP, v1.2 SPLIT** (`Ca(NO₃)₂. ‖ MS:…`, `)². ‖ Examiners…`) | **only outcome-changing delta** |
| 7 | citation drift (R1.2/DL5 → R3.1) | 700 KEEP-DL5 rows re-cite; 0 outcome changes | cosmetic |
| new | **Set P missing v1.2 `gov`/`al`** | ruling 7.32 (`Gov. Smith`) fails live | real conformance bug |

Net: reconciling the implementation to v1.2 is now a **measured, cheap** operation — one behavioral delta (δ6, 16 decisions) plus two lexicon entries — not a re-engineering project.

## §10 What held (measured, not asserted)

- **W1, the precision doctrine** — 98.12% measured split precision; 100% of false splits inside declared doors; DL3 4,367/4,367 clean; Door B 30/30 sampled clean; Door C empty.
- **The candidate filter (Layer 0)** — decimals (6,375), scientific notation (778 superscript + 14 strict), and `).` sequences (1,928) produced zero split-side errors; R0.1-style absorption works.
- **Dotted-abbreviation tails** — 646/678 keeps correct (95.3%); the six-family world of this corpus is handled.
- **Set P's page-number entries** — `pp.` 3/3.
- **The block-edge override** — 4,367 certifications, zero spec divergence.
- **The output arithmetic of v1** — 22,257 = 17,535 + 4,722 was exactly right; v2 explains *why*.

---

## §11 Recommendations (evidence-weighted; each with its measured payoff)

1. **Build the ingestion/furniture boundary first (D1/D12 decision).** 89.6% of terminator-less chunks, 39.2% of all decisions, and 33.9% of input blocks are furniture the spec was never written for. Strip furniture upstream or recognize markdown/table/diagram/label boundaries before `decide()` — the largest single lever, and it also owns the 4 recall misses the rules cannot even see (§5). This is the "where we are not even looking" complement to "where not to split".
2. **Redesign R1.2 as a two-sided rule.** Keep-side: a dotted-tail whitelist of the six observed families (`p.d. e.g. i.e. e.m.f. s.f. b.p.`) — preserves ~97% of correct keeps (646/665) and eliminates the symbol over-fire (D6). Split-side: digits and unit/variable letters must become *licensed* splits, not suppressed ones — measured payoff: **−1,976 false merges** (1,556 digit + 420 unit-letter) at the cost of ~19 lost correct keeps. This single change removes ~70% of all wrong-direction keeps.
3. **Re-scope R3.1.** 144 part-label keeps and 33 symbol-continuation keeps are wrong; the 29 correct continuations (quote-pair, parenthetical) must survive the re-scope. Measured payoff: −177 false merges.
4. **Split R1.3's namespace.** Formula-quantity (40), chemical-formula (40), acronym/label (55), caps-emphasis (20) behave differently at sentence end; 154/155 keeps are wrong. Measured payoff: ≈ −154 false merges.
5. **Repair Set P under an L3 namespace guard.** Add the missing `gov`/`al` (ruling 7.32 fails live today); resolve the four collisions (`No.` numero↔answer-word, `Ca.` circa↔element, `sat.` Saturday↔verb, `ms.` honorific↔unit) by namespace tags, not deletion — the guard also future-proofs chemistry/SI prose, which is this corpus's home turf.
6. **Close Door A(ii) with one enumerator/label rule** (OI-1 widened, as v1 recommended — now with the full family): multi-digit orphans (89), digit-letter markers (70), line-start enumerator glue (1,107), `(a–h)` 736, `Q\d+` 3,250, `MS:`/`Spec ref:`/`✓`/marks-glue. This is both a precision repair (−159 false splits) and a recall repair.
7. **Reconcile the implementation to v1.2.** Now measured: δ6 (16 decisions) + two P entries + five inert deltas. Cheap, and it makes the next trace speak v1.2's citations natively.
8. **R4.2 enumeration-ellipsis ends** (10 wrong) — fold into the ingestion/enumerator work rather than growing the ellipsis rule.

Ordered by measured payoff per unit of spec surface: **1 → 2 → 6 → 3 → 4 → 5 → 7 → 8.**

## Appendix A — Trace line format and provenance classes

- Line grammar: `^(SPLIT|KEEP)\s+(\S+)\s+@(\d+)\s+\.\.\.(.*)\.\.\.$`; context = block-relative ±25-char window, newlines space-collapsed, `...` wrappers added by the impl (L252/L400). All 12,862 windows verified against the corpus; offsets are character offsets into `prose-corpus.md` (1,693,006 chars / 1,748,367 bytes).
- Provenance classes used above:
  - **[E]** exact census — counted over the full population from the trace and/or corpus.
  - **[F]** full-population adjudication — every member read and verdicted.
  - **[S]** seed-42 sample + Wilson 95% CI (sample size stated inline).
  - **[C]** derived from implementation code control flow (line-referenced).
- Workstreams: quantitative census (§2), split-side audit (§3), R1.2 census (§4.1), small-rule forensics (§4.2–4.6), output-block pathology (§6), corpus anatomy + deltas + recall (§5, §7, §8). Machine-readable counts and full adjudicated lists were produced per workstream (re-derivable by the commands in README "How to Test" plus the stated seed).
